agency: New York City Public Schools (New York City Department of Education; legally the City School District of the City of New York)
union: United Federation of Teachers (UFT), Local 2, American Federation of Teachers
title_code_or_exam: No civil service exam. A New York State teaching certificate (Initial, or Transitional B while in an alternative program) is the qualifying credential; the state exams are the Educating All Students test and a content specialty test.

hiring.summary: The state licenses teachers and the city hires them. A candidate earns or begins earning a New York State certificate, clears state fingerprinting, applies once through TeachNYC and is then hired by an individual principal. The city runs its own background check before the teacher starts a four-year probationary appointment.

nodes.question: Which route to a state certificate?

nodes.title: Finish a registered teacher preparation program
nodes.body: The candidate completes a state-registered college program that leads to the certificate. The standalone edTPA performance exam has not been required since April 27, 2022.

nodes.title: Pass the state certification exams
nodes.body: The candidate must pass the Educating All Students test and the content exam for the subject.

lanes.label: Alternative route (New York City Teaching Fellows)

nodes.title: Complete summer pre-service training
nodes.body: Career changers and recent graduates take a seven-week summer training program and begin teaching in September.
nodes.who: Candidate; New York City Teaching Fellows; partner university

nodes.title: Teach on a Transitional B certificate
nodes.body: The Fellow teaches full time while finishing a subsidized master's degree. The certificate is valid only while the candidate stays enrolled in good standing in the program.
nodes.time: Certificate valid 3 years; certification typically in 2 to 3 years

nodes.title: Complete three required workshops
nodes.body: Candidates complete workshops on child abuse identification and reporting (two hours), school violence prevention (two hours) and the Dignity for All Students Act (at least six hours).
nodes.law: Education Law §3004(2), (3); Dignity for All Students Act training per NYSED

nodes.title: Clear state fingerprinting
nodes.body: Fingerprints are taken by the state vendor IdentoGO and run against state and FBI records. Clearance is automatic when there is no criminal history.
nodes.time: Generally within 24 hours with no record
nodes.who: Candidate; IdentoGO; state Office of School Personnel Review and Accountability

nodes.title: Apply through TeachNYC
nodes.body: Certified candidates, or those on track to be certified by September 1, file one application. Once it is accepted, principals can see it in the New Teacher Finder.
nodes.who: Candidate; New York City Public Schools recruitment office
nodes.law: Administrative process; Chancellor's authority under Education Law §2590-h

nodes.title: Interview and accept an offer from a principal
nodes.body: Candidates contact principals directly and may be asked to interview and teach a demonstration lesson. The school then nominates the new hire for its vacancy.

nodes.title: Clear the city background check
nodes.body: After the nomination, the hire completes forms in the city's Applicant Gateway, is fingerprinted again and shows proof of certification. No one may work in the schools without clearance from the Office of Personnel Investigation.
nodes.who: New hire; human resources; Office of Personnel Investigation

nodes.title: Begin a four-year probationary appointment
nodes.body: Starting pay on the current schedule (effective September 14, 2025) is $68,902 with a bachelor's degree and $77,455 with a master's. Probation is shorter for teachers with regular substitute service or tenure earned in another district. The union describes the term as four years and a day.
nodes.time: 4 years (3 years with prior tenure; as short as 2 with substitute service)

nodes.title: Tenure decision at the end of probation
nodes.body: The superintendent reports which probationers were found competent, efficient and satisfactory. A tenured teacher can then be removed only for cause.

end_to_end.text: Timelines vary. For a certified candidate the stated clocks are about 24 hours for state fingerprint clearance and 2 to 4 weeks for application review, plus however long school hiring takes. Fellows go from a seven-week summer program to teaching in September. A traditional candidate first needs about four years for a degree. Probation then runs four years.

firing.summary: How a teacher can be fired for cause depends on tenure. A probationary teacher can be let go at any time without a hearing unless the teacher proves bad faith, an unconstitutional purpose or a statutory violation. A tenured teacher can be removed only for cause after an Education Law §3020-a hearing, as modified by the UFT contract. The separate §3020-b track for ineffective ratings was repealed in 2024.

nodes.title: Superintendent discontinues probation
nodes.body: Service can be ended at any time during probation without a hearing. Courts will overturn it only if the teacher shows bad faith, an unconstitutional purpose or a violation of a statute (Matter of Frasier v Board of Education, Court of Appeals, 1988).
nodes.time: Any time; written notice at least 60 days before probation ends if tenure will be denied
nodes.law: Education Law §2573(1)(a)(ii); Frasier v Board of Educ., 71 NY2d 763 (1988)

nodes.title: Teacher may request reasons in writing
nodes.body: A teacher facing a recommendation to deny tenure or discontinue service may ask for a written statement of reasons. The district must provide it within seven days.
nodes.time: Notice 30 days before the decision; request up to 21 days before; reasons within 7 days

nodes.title: Advisory review by a committee
nodes.body: The teacher can have the discontinuance reviewed by a committee set up under the union contract or chancellor's rules, with at least one week's written notice. The committee only recommends; the decision stays with the superintendent or chancellor.
nodes.time: Notice at least 1 week before the review
nodes.who: Review committee; UFT advocate; superintendent or chancellor
nodes.law: Panel for Educational Policy bylaws §§13.4.2, 13.4.3 (approved March 12, 2025)

nodes.title: Service ends
nodes.body: The city can separately terminate the person's New York City license under Chancellor's Regulation C-31. The teacher has 15 school days to appeal and is suspended without pay while the review is pending.

nodes.title: Investigation and reassignment
nodes.body: While misconduct is investigated, the teacher can be moved to an administrative office or an administrative job in the school. In rare sexual or financial misconduct cases the teacher can be suspended. Under the contract, charges must follow within 60 days, or 15 days after an investigator's report in sexual or financial cases.
nodes.time: Charges within 60 days of reassignment; 15 days after an investigator's report in excepted cases
nodes.who: Department of Education; Office of Special Investigations or Special Commissioner of Investigation

nodes.title: Charges filed and probable cause found
nodes.body: Charges of misconduct or incompetence must be in writing and generally brought within three years of the conduct. In New York City the chancellor, not a school board, acts as the employing board and finds probable cause.
nodes.time: Probable cause within 5 days of receiving charges

nodes.title: Teacher requests a hearing
nodes.body: Not responding counts as waiving the hearing. If the teacher waives, the Panel for Educational Policy or the community superintendent decides the case and the penalty.
nodes.who: Teacher; UFT borough office and New York State United Teachers counsel
nodes.law: Education Law §3020-a(2)(f); Panel for Educational Policy bylaws §13.2

nodes.title: Hearing before one hearing officer
nodes.body: The city and union jointly assign a single hearing officer from standing panels. The contract requires a pre-hearing conference within 15 days of the hearing request and the hearing finished within 60 days after that. All evidence must be in within 125 days of the charges.
nodes.time: Pre-hearing within 15 days; hearing done within 60 days of the pre-hearing conference
nodes.who: Hearing officer; Department of Education attorneys; teacher's counsel
nodes.law: Education Law §3020-a(3); §3020(4); 2023 UFT–DOE memorandum of agreement amending Article 21

nodes.title: Decision and penalty
nodes.body: The hearing officer rules on each charge and sets any penalty: a written reprimand, a fine, unpaid suspension or dismissal. Ineffective evaluation ratings no longer create a presumption of incompetence under state law; incompetence is charged under §3020-a like other cause.
nodes.time: Within 30 days of the last hearing day
nodes.law: Education Law §3020-a(4)(a); §3020-b repealed by L. 2024, ch. 143 (June 2024)

nodes.title: Appeal to State Supreme Court
nodes.body: Either side may ask State Supreme Court to vacate or modify the decision within 10 days. An appeal does not delay the penalty.

aside.label: Not for cause
aside.text: When a teaching position is abolished, the least senior teacher in that tenure area is let go first. This is not a disciplinary firing, and neither is excessing, which moves a teacher out of a school without ending employment.

stats.text: Starting teacher salary on the schedule effective September 14, 2025: $68,902 with a bachelor's degree (column C1) and $77,455 with a master's (C2+PD).
On the schedule taking effect September 14, 2026 (a 3.5% raise), starting salary rises to $71,314 with a bachelor's and $80,166 with a master's.
More than 9,000 New York City Teaching Fellows work in the city's schools, according to the program.
One TeachNYC application reaches principals at more than 1,600 schools.

caveats: Education Law §3020-b (removal after two or three consecutive ineffective ratings) was repealed by Chapter 143 of the Laws of 2024, signed in June 2024. The firing chart therefore has no separate ratings lane. Districts may keep using §3012-d evaluation plans until a new plan is required by June 30, 2032 (per the S9054 bill page), and the UFT–DOE contract may still carry evaluation-related terms. Ask counsel how any case charged before the repeal is treated.

In New York City, §3020 lets the city and the UFT change §3020-a procedures by contract. The hearing-officer assignment, the 15-day pre-hearing conference and the 60-day reassignment rule come from the contract, not the statute. The statutory 15-day hearing-officer selection in §3020-a(3)(b)(iii) expressly does not apply in New York City.

The Article 21(G)(4) text is quoted from the 2009–2018 printable edition on uft.org, the most recent full text that could be opened. The 2023 memorandum of agreement amends Article 21 (pre-hearing conferences) but does not restate G(4). The UFT's current disciplinary-actions page describes the same 60-day and 15-day rules.

Pay during reassignment and suspension varies: the default is with pay, but unpaid suspension is allowed for certain drug felonies, for physical or sexual abuse of a student after a probable-cause finding (§3020-a(2)(b), (c); source 50) and for serious misconduct under contract Article 21(G)(5)-(6).
Two ways out sit outside this chart: resignation or retirement, and state revocation of a certificate for moral character under 8 NYCRR Part 83 (source 51), which bars teaching statewide.
Excessing is not a layoff. Since summer 2021 the city generally no longer places newly excessed teachers in the Absent Teacher Reserve (source 49).

Salary figures: the schedule in force on the compile date (September 11, 2026) is the one effective September 14, 2025. A 3.5 percent raise takes effect September 14, 2026, three days later. uft.org blocks direct downloads, so the salary table was read through a fetch tool; figures should be checked against the page before publication.

nysenate.gov blocked direct downloads for most sections (403). Statute text was read from newyork.public.law, which reproduces the nysenate.gov text and gives its last-updated date. §3020-a(2)(a) and the S9054 bill page were read directly on nysenate.gov. Typographic apostrophes in quotes were normalized to straight quotes.

Chancellor's Regulations C-31 (2002) and C-105 (2003) are the versions currently posted. C-31 still cites 'section 5.3.4' of the bylaws, which is now §13.4 of the Panel for Educational Policy bylaws approved March 12, 2025.

The bad-faith standard for probationary discontinuance is taken from the Court of Appeals decision in Matter of Frasier v Board of Educ., 71 NY2d 763 (1988), as quoted in a 2022 Commissioner's decision involving the city. The Frasier opinion itself was not opened. The same decision cites Kahn v New York City Dept. of Educ., 18 NY3d 457 (2012).
unverified: Official counts of §3020-a cases filed against New York City teachers, and how long they take: no current NYSED or city publication was found. The NYSED Teacher Tenure Hearing Unit page has no statistics. No stats line is included.

The rule that a hiring nomination expires after 60 days without fingerprinting: it appears only in a search snippet from the NYC Teaching Fellows help center, which returned 403. The TeachNYC Applicant Gateway guide and InfoHub page do not state it. It was removed from the chart.
Time for the city (Office of Personnel Investigation) background clearance: C-105 and InfoHub give no clock.
Time to evaluate prior-experience salary step credit (the prior page said about 20 weeks): the uft.org salary-steps page returned 403 to every fetch method. Removed.
Exam score turnaround (the prior page said 2 to 6 weeks): no official source was fetched. Removed.

The full text of Education Law §3020-b before repeal (day counts for the former ratings track): nysenate.gov no longer lists the section, and Justia and FindLaw returned 403. Its former terms are known only from the 2015 NYSED memo, and are no longer operative.
The current consolidated UFT–DOE contract text of Article 21 (2023–2027): the uft.org article page returned navigation only. See the caveat on the 2009–2018 edition.

How the community superintendent's discontinuance maps onto the §2573 'majority vote of the board of education' in New York City: the 2022 Commissioner's decision shows the superintendent issuing it, but no statute or regulation stating the delegation was opened.
corrections_to_prior_version: Removed the Education Law §3020-b ineffective-ratings lane. §3020-b was repealed by Chapter 143 of the Laws of 2024 (S9054/A9849, signed June 28, 2024, effective immediately). Two or three ineffective ratings no longer create a statutory presumption of incompetence; incompetence is charged under §3020-a.
Probationary review bylaw: the prior page cited Panel for Educational Policy bylaws §4.3.2 (formerly §5.3.4). The bylaws approved March 12, 2025 put it at §13.4.2, with notice rules at §13.4.3.

Probationary review timing: the prior page said a review is scheduled within about one year. That one-year limit in the bylaws (§13.4.1) applies to rating appeals, not discontinuance. Replaced it with the verified one-week notice rule.

Hearing officer: the prior page said a single officer from an American Arbitration Association panel is chosen in about 15 days. In New York City the city and UFT assign officers by mutual agreement from standing panels (2023 memorandum of agreement), and the statute's 15-day selection rule expressly does not apply to cities of one million or more.

Pre-hearing conference: the 2023 memorandum of agreement amended Article 21 to hold it within 15 days of the hearing request, with the hearing finished within 60 days and the decision due within 30 days. The prior page gave only the statute's 10 to 15 days.

Probable-cause vote under mayoral control: the prior page said the vote is 'delegated to the Chancellor.' The statute gives the power to the chancellor directly: Education Law §2590-h(38) and (38-a) make the chancellor the employing board for §3020-a, with the Panel for Educational Policy keeping cases where the hearing is waived (§2590-h(38-a); bylaws §13.2).

Citation error: the prior page cited Education Law §3004-c for fingerprinting and the city background check. §3004-c covers denial of an application for certification. Fingerprint clearance is §3035 (and §3004-b); the city check rests on §2590-h(20) and Chancellor's Regulation C-105.

Citation error: the prior page cited Education Law §2590-i for 'principal recommends staff selection.' §2590-i sets principals' duties and how principals are chosen; it does not govern teacher selection. Replaced with §2590-j(4)(a) (chancellor appoints teachers) and the TeachNYC description of school-level hiring.
Bad-faith standard pinned to Matter of Frasier v Board of Educ. of City School Dist. of City of N.Y., 71 NY2d 763 (1988), as quoted by Commissioner's Decision No. 18,212 (Nov. 22, 2022).
Added the §3031 clocks the prior page left out: 30 days' notice before the decision, a request for reasons up to 21 days before and reasons due within 7 days.
